newsitem.title: SPAIN: Amper up on talk of shareholder cash return.
newsitem.headline: Amper up on talk of shareholder cash return.

text.p: Shares in Spain's telecom equipment firm Amper were up sharply on Friday amid talk that the firm is to announce a dividend payment and a cut in the shares' face value, returning cash to shareholders, dealers said.
Strong nine-month results also pushed the share price up, dealers said.
A spokesman for Amper denied that the firm plans a nominal cut, but said plans to pay an interim dividend against 1996 results had already been announced.
At midday, Amper was up 85 pesetas or 4.3 percent to 2,055 while the Ibex-35 was up 0.47 percent to 4,532.99.
"The buzz is that at the next board meeting they're going to approve a dividend payment, and they're also going to reduce the face value of the shares," said a trader at Argentaria brokerage.

Dealers at several brokerages in Madrid said rumours were circulating that Amper was to approve an interim dividend of 50 pesetas gross, and was to cut the nominal value of the shares by 100 pesetas, returning the cash to shareholders.
"The chairman said at the last shareholders' meeting that (Amper) would pay an interim dividend before the year-end," an Amper spokesman told Reuters.
But a cut in the face value of the shares "does not enter into the company's plans at the moment," he added.
The next board meeting is set for November 27.
In the first nine months of the year, Amper's net profit rose 48 percent to 3.05 billion pesetas.
